intro: Brighton & Hove Albion have signed Canada striker Promise David from Belgian side Royale Union Saint-Gilloise on a season-long loan that includes an obligation to buy, according to BBC Sport. The agreement is reported to carry a purchase obligation worth £22m, a figure the media outlet cites in its coverage.

sections.heading: Deal details: what the club and report have confirmed
sections.text:
The transfer involves Promise David moving from Royale Union Saint-Gilloise to Brighton on a season-long loan with an obligation to buy, as reported by BBC Sport. The reporting identifies a reported fee of £22m attached to the obligation to buy. Beyond the headline terms — the loan length, the obligation to buy and the reported financial figure — the coverage cited does not provide additional granular contract specifics in the public report.

As with many modern transfers, the structure combines an initial loan element with a guaranteed future purchase obligation. Media reports frequently use such structures for accounting, sporting and regulatory reasons; in this case the obligation to buy means a subsequent permanent transfer is expected to follow the loan period under the agreed terms reported by BBC Sport.
